rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Adam and his descendants revelation alongside nature and intellect as a weapon for combating Satan.
rows.anchor: This actually is the weapon which God had blessed Adam (sws) and his progeny with.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's Book is the sole protection from Satan's attacks; without it people remain vulnerable to devils among jinn and humankind.
rows.anchor: the sole means to remain secure from the onslaughts of Satan in this world is the Book of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam was a prophet sent to counter Satan, so God must have revealed a sharīʿah suited to his circumstances; Islahi refers to directives under Abel and Cain.
rows.anchor: Adam (sws) was a prophet. He has been sent in this world to counter the onslaughts of Satan for which God’s guidance for both Adam (sws) and his progeny is essential

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression maʿīshatan ḍankan denotes a life without peace of mind or inner satisfaction.
rows.anchor: refers to a life devoid of peace of mind and inner satisfaction

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only faith in God fills the human inner vacuum; worldly resources offer temporary joy but cannot relieve spiritual anxiety, while true firm faith brings satisfaction.
rows.anchor: Similar is the case with a human being.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion concerns people with true faith, not everyone who merely claims faith; outwardly comfortable unbelievers may conceal inner threats, doubts, and fears.
rows.anchor: the discussion is not with those who merely lay claim to faith but with those who have true faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hidden spiritual distress may be visible only to the person or to people with faith-based insight, despite an appearance of happiness.
rows.anchor: Only they themselves can see them or those who have the insight of faith in them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's remembrance clears the faculties of sight, hearing, and intellect; those who evade it are spiritually blind, deaf, and intellectually deprived despite possessing these faculties.
rows.anchor: removes hurdles from the faculties of sight, hearing

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human faculties were given to recognize the signs throughout creation, not to become enslaved to what is merely tangible; failing to perceive the obvious leaves a person understanding nothing.
rows.anchor: These favours were not given to people so that they become slaves of what is palpable and tangible

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent contrast with Qāf 50:22 is resolved because people fail to recognize their blindness in earthly life but will recognize it when reality is unveiled at Judgement.
rows.anchor: The answer is that there is no discrepancy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the word glossed here means to ignore, Islahi says the ignored revelations leave the people's eyes shut and their complaint useless.
rows.anchor: They remain shut. Their complaint is of no use.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they ignored God's revelations, they deserve to be ignored in return; their complaint cannot undo that fate.
rows.anchor: Their complaint is of no use.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rendered as exceeding means to go beyond the limits.
rows.anchor: The word إ means “to exceed the limits.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who exceed limits waste their talents on things they should avoid and neglect what they were required to do.
rows.anchor: people who wasted their talents in the very things they had to abstain from

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question means that the destruction of earlier nations should have been enough to open the opponents' eyes and guide them.
rows.anchor: enough to open their eyes and give them guidance?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruins of ʿĀd and Thamūd lay along trade routes and were blatant signs; Arab poets versified their cities' destruction, and sensible people learn from others' fate.
rows.anchor: A sensible person is one who learns from the fate of others

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression is grammatically coordinated to the preceding term; the verse answers the demand for a sign of punishment.
rows.anchor: is coordinated to m . This verse answers the demand of showing a sign of punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is delayed according to God's established practice and prescribed term, not because the warning is a bluff or God lacks the means; Islahi cites the same subject in al-Shūrā.
rows.anchor: No one should think that this is a bluff or God does not have the resources to bring it about.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior divine decree means God has fixed a time for punishment, and the appointed term has a precise arrival time rather than an ambiguous one.
rows.anchor: In God’s calendar, its time of arrival is fixed to the second.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to endure his opponents' words and be diligent in prayer; prayer most effectively implants the belief that events occur by God's will for the greater good.
rows.anchor: The greatest and most effective means to fully implant this belief in one’s mind is the prayer.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's practice crystallizes the prayer timings.
rows.anchor: The Prophet (sws) has crystallized these timings through his own practice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is the Qur'an's teacher as well as its reciter.
rows.anchor: he was also its teacher.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is stressed as a means of acquiring perseverance.
rows.anchor: the prayer is stressed upon as a means to acquire perseverance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Difficult circumstances require diligence in optional prayers as well as obligatory ones.
rows.anchor: it is not merely the obligatory prayers which are needed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day's margins refer to chāsht, ẓuhr, and maghrib; ẓuhr is also a boundary because it divides the day in two.
rows.anchor: Deliberation shows that ẓuhr too is at the boundary since the day is divided into two by it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the claim that Qur'anic prayer times are absent: it mentions obligatory prayer and also tahajjud and ishrāq.
rows.anchor: This verse clearly negates the view of those people who claim that the timings

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet delineates each prayer's details, including its extent and limits.
rows.anchor: it was his task to delineate all these details

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the difficult phase of the truth's struggle with evil, prayer equips the Prophet and the ummah to persevere and merit God's help.
rows.anchor: the struggle between truth and evil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In individual or collective hardship, tahajjud and ishrāq should also be maintained, although they are optional in ordinary circumstances; Islahi says this is corroborated by Qur'an, prophetic sayings, and righteous practice.
rows.anchor: in challenging and difficult circumstances, whether they are individual or collective, these prayers must be adhered to as well

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing phrase promises that persistence and prayer will bring the Prophet abundant success in this world and the next; the phrase is compared with al-Ḍuḥā 93:5.
rows.anchor: In verse 5 of S ūrah al-Ḍuḥā, it is similarly said

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayers contain all the Prophet needs, so he need not look to anyone else for support.
rows.anchor: and there is no need for him to look up to anyone else.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told not to worry over the wealthy; their refusal is their own deprivation, and God does not need their resources.
rows.anchor: God does not need their wealth and resources.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly resources refer to Quraysh's political elites in Mecca and Ṭāʾif, who offered wealth if the Prophet would stop preaching; his concern for them came from sincere compassion, not greed.
rows.anchor: instead of accepting it, he recited before them some verses

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly wealth and resources are God's bestowals, not simply inheritance or personal intelligence, and test whether their recipients are grateful.
rows.anchor: they are God’s bestowal and by it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression about worldly life's adornment is a circumstantial accusative; worldly resources are transient and should be used to earn for the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: Such accusative of states are common in eloquent Arabic and many examples of it have been pointed out in this exegesis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealth's brightness soon fades; its proper use is to earn for the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: Its brightness will whither away soon and leave it scarred.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about testing people with worldly favors refers to God's established practice: hardship tests patience and favor tests gratitude; wealth is a trial, not an entitlement.
rows.anchor: When He inflicts them with hardships, the purpose is to test their patience and when He blesses them with favours, the purpose is to test how grateful they are.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and his companions need no patronage from ungrateful elites because God's provision will be far better and everlasting, unlike their brief worldly wealth.
rows.anchor: It will never fa de away.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety grows from the nourishment God revealed; trying to cultivate it with stagnant water is unnatural and yields vice rather than virtue.
rows.anchor: if it seemingly does grow, then it will bear fruits of vice and not virtue.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl has a wider Arabic meaning than the Prophet's household: it includes people related to someone and can denote a prophet's nation, as shown by lexicography and usage.
rows.anchor: it has a wider connotation.

rows.speaker: Abu Bakr (rta)
rows.claim: A report from Abū Bakr uses ahl broadly: when asked whom he appointed over Muslims, he answered that he appointed the best ahl.
rows.anchor: Abu Bakr (rta) that when on the day of Judgement his Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ismāʿīl's command to his ahl to observe prayer and zakāh means those associated with him, not only his wife and children.
rows.anchor: all those associated to him are meant.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse ahl includes every believer in Muḥammad, whether kin or not, Quraysh or Hashimite, enslaved or free, man or woman; this use raises the standing of poor Muslims as the Prophet's family.
rows.anchor: Muslims regardless of belonging to the Quraysh or the Hashimites

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must maintain prayer and direct his followers to do likewise; this is the vigilant prayer already described in the preceding verse, which builds perseverance.
rows.anchor: The prayer here refers to the same prayer mentioned in the previous verse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to persevere in prayer pictures a farmer tilling, sowing, watering, and guarding his land until it yields blessings.
rows.anchor: just as a farmer tills his soil, sows deeds, waters it and continues to guard it, the Prophet (sws) too should tend to his land

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises livelihood to the Prophet and his followers so he can continue his task and prayer without anxiety about provision; Jesus is reported to say that a laborer deserves his hire.
rows.anchor: Jesus (sws) is reported to have said: “The labourer is worthy of his hire.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular pronoun for God's providing for the Prophet addresses him as head of the whole Muslim family, so the promise includes all Muslims; in the Islamic political system the ruler provides for the community.
rows.anchor: This address to the Prophet (sws) is in his capacity of the head of the Islamic family and its sustainer.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar exemplified responsibility for their people; ʿUmar felt accountable even if a dog died hungry in a distant part of his realm and acted to prevent such suffering.
rows.anchor: did not merely express these emotions but took practical steps

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After promising worldly sustenance, the verse gives the Hereafter's glad tidings: only the pious attain ultimate success.
rows.anchor: In the previous part of the verse, promise for worldly sustenance was made; now glad tidings of success in the hereafter are given

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's guarantee of provision cannot be conveyed to those who lack its true experience; only people who taste its essence can know what it contains, and Islahi says he has seen devout examples in life and history.
rows.anchor: Only experience can convince a person

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When opponents were cornered in argument, they demanded a sign, meaning a miracle or the threatened punishment; People of the Book were especially responsible and encouraged idolaters to ask for what earlier messengers showed.
rows.anchor: When the Prophet’s adversaries would feel helpless and cornered in countering him through arguments, as a last resort, they would demand from a sign of him being God’s envoy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book are answered first: the advent of the last Messenger, predicted in their scriptures and confirming those prophecies, is already a sufficient sign.
rows.anchor: the last messenger whose advent was predicted in their scriptures

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fulfillment of the scriptural prophecies about the last Messenger is the sign called bayyina in this verse.
rows.anchor: the last messenger whose advent was predicted in their scriptures has now come

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following verse answers the idolaters by saying that God sent a messenger to remove their excuse for demanding a prior warning.
rows.anchor: in order to do away with their excuse mentioned in the verse, God sent a

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer is divided between the verses: this verse answers the People of the Book, and the next answers the idolaters.
rows.anchor: In this verse, the first

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final warning shifts from the indirect address of the preceding two verses to direct address, signaling the intensity of anger; a parallel clause is omitted because contextual indications make it clear.
rows.anchor: In this verse, the address has become direct to express the intensity of anger.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening warns Qur'an opponents of God's grasp and the Hereafter's horrors: associating partners without basis and following Satan leads to doom, since Satan guides followers toward Hell.
rows.anchor: Satan’s real task, for which God has given him respite, is not to provide guidance so that people follow him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human development and earth's revival after drought argue for resurrection; doubters should reflect on themselves and the world instead of demanding to see punishment, since the Hereafter necessarily follows from God's attributes.
rows.anchor: Arguments in favour of the Hereafter are cited by referring to phases of creation of a human being and by the phenomenon of earth’s revival to life after a dry spell.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claiming to worship God while associating partners with Him is baseless.
rows.anchor: the claim of worshipping God while associating partners with Him is a baseless one

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite described in the passage worships and obeys God only while apparent benefits continue, then flees in trial to seek help elsewhere and loses both this world and the next.
rows.anchor: people who were indifferent to the Hereafter and wanted to always argue and dispute with the Prophet (sws) in support of polytheism

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged deities sought for benefit cause more harm than good; only God has authority to harm or benefit people.
rows.anchor: The harm of those to whom they run for their benefits while leaving God is more than their use.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever loses hope that God will help him may attempt to reach the heavens, but his greatest scheme cannot solve the problem.
rows.anchor: If someone loses hope in God, he can try to reach the heavens if the greatest of his schemes can solve this problem.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows everyone's behavior and all cases ultimately come before His justice; He distinguishes callers to monotheism from those who distorted religion through innovations, sending disbelievers to Hell and the faithful to Paradise.
rows.anchor: God is aware of everyone’s behaviour. None of a person’s word or deed is hidden from Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage explains the true objective of Abraham's religion and the building of God's House.
rows.anchor: The real objective of Abraham’s (sws) religion and of building the House of God is explained.

rows.speaker: Zamakhasharī
rows.claim: Zamakhasharī regards the sūrah as Makkan except for a few verses.
rows.anchor: Zamakhashar ī too has regarded this sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destroyed peoples' surviving buildings are a lesson for anyone with insight, but hearts that have become blind cannot be healed.
rows.anchor: were the remnants of the magnificent buildings they built. They are enough to learn a lesson from if a person has the eye.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those demanding an accelerated doom should remember that God's calendar differs from theirs; a divine day equals a thousand earth years, and God's promise will come after the respite He gave earlier nations.
rows.anchor: His one day is equal to a thousand earth years. For this reason, they should not ask to hasten this doom.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Messenger's role is to warn people and give glad tidings; the decision to send punishment belongs to God.
rows.anchor: The purpose of a Messenger is to warn people and deliver them glad tidings. The decision to send punishment is in the Hands of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's opposition is no novelty: devils impede messengers who try to reform affairs, but God removes Satan's effects and makes His word prevail.
rows.anchor: Whenever a prophet or a messenger has tried to show courage against these adversities and reform affairs, devils have always tried to impede this

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God allows satanic propaganda to distinguish sincere believers from false claimants: truth-seekers' faith grows while hypocrites and the wretched go astray, and God assigns Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: The reason that God has given these devils this opportunity is to distinguish true believers from false claimants.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Migrants and those preparing to migrate are promised success in this world and the next, confirmed by God's attributes and signs in creation.
rows.anchor: Glad tidings of success in both this world and the next are given to people who had migrated by that time or were preparing to do so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' respite reflects God's haste in mercy and deferral of torment; the Prophet should leave their matter to God, who will judge them in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: God shows haste in mercy and defers torment. The Prophet (sws) is directed to consign their matter to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage delivers a final refutation of polytheism and intercession: the deities and mediators will not help idolaters before God.
rows.anchor: the deities and intercessors on the basis of whom they are unmindful of the Hereafter will not be of the slightest benefit to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conclusion collectively directs Muslims to strive for God's cause as heirs of Abraham's religion, bear witness to truth, maintain prayer, and hold fast to God as guardian and helper.
rows.anchor: They are told that they are now the inheritors of Abraham’s religion. God has given them the title of Muslims.
